transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (CISO, Arclight), Dev Patel (Security Engineer), Hannah Ross (Platform Lead), Carlos Vega (Compliance).

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I think we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar. Quick intro, and Priya will cover the pen-test findings and remediation path.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Hey, thanks. We wanted to go through the pen test results you sent last week and make sure the patching cadence and SDLC controls line up with our audit window.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Yep, absolutely. I'll start with a short recap — Redwood engaged an external firm, RedOak Sec, scoped hosted and dedicated endpoints plus control plane access, ran both authenticated and unauthenticated tests. We had a mix of findings: a couple of criticals (mainly misconfig/upgradeable libs in an internal admin tool), some highs around missing rate-limits on a debug endpoint, and a few medium/low items.
[00:45] Dev Patel: Quick clarifying Q — the admin tool, is that in the customer-managed plane or part of Redwood's control plane? I think the report's text is ambiguous.
[00:54] Priya Nair: Good call — that's our internal admin microservice that runs in the Redwood control plane for tenant routing, not customer-managed. We did have one instance running an older dependency in a staging pool that RedOak hit during authenticated tests.
[01:10] Hannah Ross: So that's strictly Redwood-side, correct? We just want to know which side we need to patch or if it affects our SLAs.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Correct, that's Redwood. We patched the dependency in staging within 48 hours and rolled the fix to canary the next day. Priya can go through the remediation timeline.
[01:26] Priya Nair: Timeline: patch discovered 2026-04-12, hotfix to staging 2026-04-14, canary deployment 2026-04-15, full rollout 2026-04-18. We also validated via internal CI and smoke tests. We flagged the issue as ticket RED-4532 in our vuln tracker.
[01:42] Dev Patel: What's the process for verification — will RedOak retest or do you provide an evidence package? We need traces for our auditors.
[01:50] Jordan Lee: We can provide the remediation evidence package — CVE mitigations, commit IDs, container image hashes, deployment timestamps, and CI run artifacts. RedOak can do a retest on the specific findings; we recommend a targeted retest rather than full-scope for efficiency.
[02:06] Maya Chen: We typically require a third-party retest for criticals within our audit period. We will need confirmation that the fix is deployed in prod and a retest window.
[02:14] Priya Nair: Understood, we'll coordinate with RedOak and share a proposed retest window week of 2026-05-18.
[02:22] Carlos Vega: On the topic of audit evidence, what's your log retention for tenant-level audit logs and admin actions? Our compliance needs 12 months retention and exportability.
[02:31] Priya Nair: For hosted customers, default audit logs retention is 90 days in the console. For enterprise, we support configurable retention and can push logs to a customer-owned S3 or SIEM with retention policies — we've done 12+ month retention setups for other banks. We'll send sample configs.
[02:46] Hannah Ross: Is that export via agent or push? We have strict egress rules.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Push via secure, authenticated transfer to your S3 with cross-account role. Or if preferred, we can also support VPC Flow to your SIEM endpoint.
[02:58] Dev Patel: About KMS — how are keys managed for customer data at rest? Are you using customer-managed keys (CMKs)? We've got a policy to only use CMKs for production.
[03:07] Priya Nair: We support both Redwood-managed CMKs and customer-managed keys in AWS KMS/HSM integrations. For Private deployments we can use your HSM. We'll include the KMS key policy and envelope encryption flow in the artifacts.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Good. Also want to cover RBAC and SSO — we saw a note about admin users having broad roles during canary. Can you confirm your RBAC model and SSO integrations?
[03:28] Jordan Lee: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with least-privilege roles out of the box: owner, admin, operator, viewer. The admin role is limited to tenant-level config; control-plane admin access is separate and goes through Redwood IAM with stricter controls and just-in-time access for maintenance.
[03:44] Dev Patel: Any time-based access or session re-validation for admin console? That's part of our internal policies.
[03:49] Priya Nair: We have session timeouts, and for control-plane operations we require MFA and break-glass approvals. We log all sudo-like actions and can provide a stream of the audit events.
[03:59] Maya Chen: About patch cadence — what's your typical cadence for rolling OS and library upgrades across the fleet? We need to map to our vulnerability SLA: criticals remediated within 7 days, highs within 30.
[04:10] Priya Nair: We have a triage process: critical CVEs trigger immediate hotfix workflows; we target remediation within 72 hours for criticals where possible, otherwise we schedule a canary then full rollout. For high severity, we aim for 30 days. There's sometimes drift for third-party model infra where compatibility testing is needed, and we coordinate with customers for maintenance windows for Private deployments.
[04:32] Dev Patel: Can you share SLAs / runbooks for the hotfix process? We need to include them in our internal risk register.
[04:37] Jordan Lee: We'll include the runbook and an example remediation ticket lifecycle exported from our vuln management system.
[04:44] Hannah Ross: How do you avoid regressions in models and runtime when you patch low-level libs? Our inference workloads are sensitive.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Good question — we have a special compatibility pipeline: after a patch build, we run model-regression evals with a representative prompt set, KV/cache warmup tests, and perf benchmarks. If we detect latency regressions or correctness issues, we hold the rollout and engage the model team. We can share the test criteria.
[05:11] Maya Chen: For Private deployments, what's the recommended cadence? We can't accept weekly restarts.
[05:16] Priya Nair: For Private/on-prem, we recommend quarterly maintenance with emergency hotfix paths. We try to bundle non-critical updates to minimize restarts; critical patches are treated as exceptions and scheduled with the customer's downtime window.
[05:29] Dev Patel: Back to the pen test findings — what were the misconfig items we should care about for tenant isolation?
[05:35] Priya Nair: The report called out a couple of misconfig flags in the routing layer for a small subset of legacy tenants that allowed overly permissive metadata queries. We closed those by patching the flag and rolling a config enforcement rule to the router, and added a unit test to the CI to prevent regression.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Good to hear. We'll want the unit test and CI artifact as proof.
[05:58] Priya Nair: We'll attach the CI job link and test logs.
[06:02] Carlos Vega: Does Redwood provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications? Our procurement requires both.
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Yes, we maintain SOC 2 Type II and are ISO 27001 certified. We can share the latest reports under an NDA/secure portal.
[06:15] Carlos Vega: And do you produce a managed audit log package for our auditors or do we need to pull raw logs?
[06:21] Liam Ortiz: We can produce a packaged export with a manifest and sign-off; typically customers pull raw logs to their SIEM but we also generate a forensics-ready bundle if needed.
[06:30] Dev Patel: One thing in the pen-test PDF: there's a weak TLS config callout on one test host, maybe staging. Can you confirm TLS versions enforced in prod?
[06:38] Priya Nair: All prod endpoints enforce TLS 1.2 minimum, prefer 1.3. That weak TLS instance was a staging host with a legacy test harness — we removed it after triage.
[06:47] Hannah Ross: Are there any single-tenant database backups containing PII that we should be aware of for data residency?
[06:54] Priya Nair: For hosted tenants, we do ephemeral caches for model context and don't persist prompt-level PII by default; customers can opt-in to longer retention. Backups for dedicated/private deployments can be configured to stay in-region and encrypted with CMKs. We'll include our data residency mapping in the artifact.
[07:12] Maya Chen: On remediation proof, we'll need: commit hash, image digest, deployment time, and RedOak retest sign-off for criticals.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: Noted — we'll package that into the remediation tracker.
[07:24] Dev Patel: How do you handle vulnerability disclosure from external researchers? Any bug-bounty or coord disclosure process?
[07:30] Priya Nair: We have a coordinated disclosure program and a triage email; no public bug bounty yet but we pay discretionary bounties and we route reports to the security ops team with SLA for acknowledgement within 48 hours.
[07:42] Carlos Vega: For our compliance artifacts we also need the secure SDLC evidence — threat modeling, code review enforcement, and dependency scanning results. Do you have a standard package?
[07:52] Priya Nair: Yes — we can provide snapshot exports: threat model for the routing stack, code review policy (mandatory PR approvals + automated scans), SCA outputs (Snyk/OSS scan reports) and CI gating rules.
[08:03] Hannah Ross: Can you explain the KMS envelope flow quickly? We need to map where plaintext keys live.
[08:08] Priya Nair: Sure — data encryption: tenant data is encrypted with a data key generated per-tenant; that data key is encrypted with the KMS CMK (customer-managed or Redwood-managed). The KMS only holds encrypted DEKs; plaintext keys are never written to disk. For Private we can integrate with your HSM and rotate per your policy.
[08:26] Dev Patel: Rotation frequency and auditability?
[08:28] Priya Nair: Rotation is configurable, default 90 days for our managed keys; we log rotation events and key usage metrics to the audit stream. We'll include sample logs.
[08:37] Maya Chen: What about secrets management for model weights and credentials? Are those in Vault?
[08:41] Priya Nair: Yes, secrets are stored in a secret manager (HashiCorp Vault for our Private deployments and AWS Secrets Manager for hosted) with access policies and short TTLs for ephemeral credentials.
[08:51] Dev Patel: For the high severity finding around rate-limiting, did you add rate-limits or WAF rules?
[08:56] Priya Nair: We added a WAF rule to block the debug endpoint from external customers and added rate-limiting at the edge. We also updated the endpoint to require explicit auth and wrote integration tests.
[09:10] Hannah Ross: Are those WAF rules publishable so we can align with our threat intel?
[09:14] Priya Nair: We can share the rule IDs and a redacted rule set.
[09:18] Dev Patel: About the vuln tracker, do you use a public issue tracker or an internal system? We need to cross-reference tickets.
[09:24] Priya Nair: Internal tracker (PhantomSec) — but we can export CSVs of tickets for customers with redacted info as needed.
[09:31] Jordan Lee: Quick recap — Arclight needs the remediation tracker, CI artifacts, audit log samples, architecture/KMS flow, and to schedule a retest week of 2026-05-18. Anything else?
[09:42] Maya Chen: Also include your hotfix runbook and the compatibility test criteria for patches that touch runtime libs.
[09:48] Priya Nair: Will do.
[09:51] Carlos Vega: One last procurement question — any third-party dependencies that are end-of-life and could be a long-term risk?
[09:57] Priya Nair: We maintain a third-party inventory; nothing EOL in prod, we do quarterly reviews and have an upgrade queue. We'll share the inventory snapshot.
[10:06] Dev Patel: Okay thanks. We'll compile the list of critical/high items we want prioritized for retest.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: Great — action items we captured in the doc; we'll follow up via the secure link. Thanks all.
[10:18] Meeting end.

Notes: transcripts include occasional filler and slight name mismatches in auto-transcription. References: pen-test report (RedOak_Summary_2026-04-10.pdf), remediation tracker (RED-4532 export), KMS_flow_v1.pdf, audit_log_samples.zip.
